In the Prophet Joseph Smith’s time, definitions of the wordsblackandblacknessincluded “darkness,” “destitute of light,” and “atrociously wicked” (Noah Webster,An American Dictionary of the English Language[1828], “Black,” “Blackness”). Elsewhere in the book of Moses, the wordblacknesswas associated with a lack of spiritual light. When Joseph Smith first recorded the revelations in the book of Moses, the wordblacknesswas used to describe Moses’s encounter with Satan inMoses 1:15. Moses asked Satan, “Where is thy glory, for it is blackness unto me? And I can judge between thee and God” (Visions of Moses, June 1830 [Moses 1],1,josephsmithpapers.org; spelling and punctuation modernized). The wordblacknesswas changed todarknessin later editions (seeMoses 1:15). The wordsblackandblacknessmay have different meanings in other scripture passages. For example, “the Book of Mormon states that ‘a skin of blackness’ [2 Nephi 5:21] came upon the Lamanites after the Nephites separated from them. The nature and appearance of this mark are not fully understood. The mark initially distinguished the Lamanites from the Nephites. Later, as both the Nephites and Lamanites went through periods of wickedness and righteousness, the mark became irrelevant” (Topics and Questions, “Race and The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints,” Gospel Library).
